stage: S4 bounded Direct Lockdown TCP TLS1.2 installation substrate
earlierReferenceFailure: Owned reference root initially inherited a default OpenSSL BasicConstraints extension twice; explicit owned root configuration fixed the generator. These attempts are retained, not claimed passing.
implementation: One caller-owned detached client operation uses numeric IPv4/IPv6 BSD sockets, fixed byte/deadline budgets, nonblocking poll and a cancellation wake pipe.
Existing StartSession FD is upgraded in place. TLS1.2 only, actual SecIdentity, explicit device DER pin and root-only BasicX509 date evaluation without network fetch.
Session tickets and renegotiation/false-start are disabled; random cache peer ID and fresh auth-break plus post-handshake actual trust recheck prevent resumed trust bypass.
All three service channels require real mutual TLS. Missing/false EnableServiceSSL is typed unsupported for this direct TCP provider.

Actual AFC stat/open/write/close ACKs and sequence/layout checks stream opaque artifact chunks, compare their actual SHA256 before Upgrade, and never perform a second whole-IPA file read or inventory.
A real beforeUpgradeSubmission hook carries only actual upload/identity/path facts; after its durable caller action cancellation/deadline are checked again before any Upgrade frame write.
A separate beforeUploadCreation planned-path event runs before FileOpen; durable journal failure or cancellation is rechecked before any remote file creation attempt.

Pre-submission errors and errors after actual Complete attempt Close/Remove on only the same live authenticated AFC, within the original cancellation/deadline. Cleanup precedes stream disposal and retains original error plus separate cleanup errors and actual removal facts.
Errors after beginning Upgrade write conservatively retain upgradeMayHaveExecuted; independent recovery API opens fresh authenticated connections and sends only Lookup.
Success requires real Complete, exact Lookup bundle/version, owned staging Remove ACK and same SessionID Stop ACK. Lookup never authenticates the installed profile or archive bytes.
Controlled loopback peer uses actual SecIdentity keys/certificates and TLS on both sides. GCD peer workers avoid starving the Swift cooperative executor with waiting listeners.
reusablePeerInterface: Fixture.withPeer(mode, bytes:actualOwnedIPAData?, bundle:String, version:String) { Context in ... }; Context.upgrade(beforeSubmission:), lookup(), endpoint/pairing/archive/date/observed.snapshot.
recoveryPeerMode: disconnectAfterUpgradeThenRecover: receive first real Upgrade then close FD; fresh second Lockdown/IP channels accept only Lookup; 1 Upgrade and 1 Lookup, 5 fresh mutually authenticated TLS channels.
limitations: Only ignored work sources exist. No canonical source/CI/docs/Git or cloud changes in this S4 stage.
Grammar4/0 is not Apple SDK compilation/typechecking. Native7 definitions have not executed; the 13 Python/OpenSSL socket cases are explicitly independent reference evidence.
Deprecated public SecureTransport iOS17 SDK acceptance and actual TLS interoperability still require the next centralized SDK gate.
The direct TCP TLS1.2 route is limited: no RemotePairing/CDTunnel/usbmux provider, no legacy SSL/TLS fallback, no plaintext AFC/installation_proxy services.
Production caller must own and serialize its transaction, validate actual signed package/profile/device authority separately, and bridge only its immutable controlled artifact.

Cancellation, deadline, broken AFC or interrupted submitted Upgrade may leave its uniquely named owned remote staging file. Ending AFC reclaims open handles, not files. The planned-path event permits caller journaling; failure facts expose path/creationAttempted/cleanupAttempted/cleanupErrors/removalVerified. A future authenticated journal-owned cleanup-only recovery route is still unfinished.
Lookup matching identifier/version cannot establish that a particular renewed profile or archive is installed, or that relaunch/data preservation succeeded.

Generic pairing CA/device pin trust is not Apple installation authority or proof of the same physical device. No-VPN same-device route, real pairing, actual install and unattended renewal remain unverified.
